challenges.name: copies-references-const-quiz
challenges.title: Copies, references and what compiles
challenges.description: Read each snippet the way the compiler does: which names are copies, which are aliases, and which initializations and assignments the language accepts.

questions.explanation: for (auto s : v) gives s a copy of each element, so the loop changes three copies and v stays [5, 6, 7]. bump takes its parameter by value: it changes a copy of v[0], so v[0] stays 5. bump_ref takes double&, so s is another name for v[1] and v[1] becomes 7. auto x = v[2] deduces double (auto drops the reference), so x is a copy and x += 1.0 does not touch v. auto& y = v[2] is an alias, so y += 0.5 makes v[2] 7.5. Result: [5, 7, 7.5]. [6, 7, 8] would need the range-for to change the elements; [5, 6, 7] ignores that bump_ref and y are references; [5, 7, 8.5] treats auto x as a reference; [6, 8, 8.5] treats every name as a reference.

questions.question: Each option is a complete small program compiled with g++ -std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra. Which of them compile? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: int seats = 39.9; compiles: copy initialization with = silently converts the double and seats is 39 (no warning under -Wall -Wextra; -Wconversion would warn). long long total{count}; compiles: int to long long is a widening conversion, every int value fits, so braces accept it. int avg{7.75}; is rejected: braces refuse a narrowing conversion, and g++ reports error: narrowing conversion of '7.75e+0' from 'double' to 'int'. Assigning v[0] = 0.0 through a const std::vector<double>& is an error (assignment of read-only location): const& promises the function will not change the caller's data. add_bonus(9.0, 0.5) with a double& parameter is an error (cannot bind non-const lvalue reference of type 'double&' to an rvalue of type 'double'): a non-const reference must refer to an existing object it can change, and 9.0 is a temporary.

options.text: int main() { int seats = 39.9; return seats; }
int main() { int count = 32; long long total{count}; return static_cast<int>(total); }
int main() { int avg{7.75}; return avg; }

void add_bonus(double& s, double b) { s += b; }
int main() { add_bonus(9.0, 0.5); }

challenges.name: apply-bonus-curve-in-place
challenges.title: Apply the exam board's bonus in place
challenges.description: The exam board grants every student in a class the same bonus. Write apply_curve(std::vector<double>& scores, double bonus), which adds the bonus to every score in the caller's vector, caps each result at 10.0 and returns how many scores actually changed, and average(const std::vector<double>& scores), which returns the class mean as a double. The test runner reads the bonus and the class list from stdin, calls both functions and prints every curved score with 1 decimal, the number of changed scores and the average with 2 decimals.

tests.name: Example from the task: +0.5, one score capped, one already at 10.0
Bonus 0.0 changes nothing and the average keeps its decimals
+1.0 bonus: scores above 9.0 are capped at 10.0, not past it
+0.3 bonus on six students, one capped and one already at 10.0
+2.0 bonus on two students, including a score of 0.0
